pcre.preg_match.doc: preg_match($pattern, $subject, $matches, $flags, $offset): result, $matches, preg_last_error() and the warning; with "matches": false, $matches is left out of the call

pcre.preg_replace.doc: preg_replace($pattern, $replacement, $subject, $limit, $count) with string or array arguments

pcre.preg_replace_callback.doc: preg_replace_callback($pattern, fn ($m) => '<n>', $subject, $limit, $count, $flags): the result, $count and every array the callback received

deviations.php: PHP runs patterns in the PCRE2 JIT with a 192 KiB stack (pcre.jit=1, applies to every preg_* function): deep recursion and long runs of group repetitions fail with PREG_JIT_STACKLIMIT_ERROR after a number of iterations set by the words the JIT's code keeps on that stack, and pcre.backtrack_limit or a pattern's (*LIMIT_MATCH=n) counts the steps where that code calls count_match()
deviations.reason: php_std keeps the same words (allocate_stack() in pcre2_jit_compile.c: groups, alternatives, captures, BRAZERO, iterators, counted loops, recursions, assertions, atomic frames, marks and THEN traps), counts the same steps and searches start positions the same way (fast_forward_first_n_chars()); this is checked by comparing, for some 50,000 generated patterns, the smallest (*LIMIT_MATCH=n) with which PHP and php_std give each result. Callouts ((?C), which PHP never calls) are left out of the compiled pattern, so a pattern with a callout can run out of stack or steps at a different point

deviations.php: (*LIMIT_HEAP=n) limits the interpreter's frame memory; PHP reuses one match data block across calls, so whether a small limit is hit depends on earlier calls
deviations.reason: Not modelled: php_std parses (*LIMIT_HEAP=n) and ignores it

deviations.php: (*UTF) without the u modifier: PHP passes PCRE2_NO_UTF_CHECK, so an invalid UTF-8 subject is undefined behaviour in PCRE2
deviations.reason: php_std does not reproduce undefined behaviour; patterns starting with (*UTF) are fuzzed with valid UTF-8 subjects

deviations.php: With UTF enabled only by the (*UTF) verb (no /u modifier), PHP advances one byte after an empty match, so the next attempt starts inside a multi-byte character with PCRE2_NO_UTF_CHECK set: PCRE2 documents this as undefined behaviour, and the results differ between CPUs and JIT targets (a lone continuation byte may be matched).
deviations.reason: No single answer exists to reproduce. The `utf_start` fuzz profiles use ASCII subjects, where no offset falls inside a character; UTF matching of multi-byte subjects is covered by the /u profiles, where PHP advances whole characters.

quirks.description: (*NOTEMPTY) is ignored when PHP calls pcre2_jit_match() (no UTF check needed) and honoured by pcre2_match() (the interpreter, or the JIT after a UTF check)

Called with only $pattern and $subject, preg_match() has no $matches and treats an empty match like preg_match_all() does: it retries at the same position with PCRE2_NOTEMPTY_ATSTART | PCRE2_ANCHORED (in the interpreter), and when that retry hits a limit the result is false. Passing $flags or $offset by name gives it a $matches to fill, which turns this off
quirks.case: pcre.json#preg_match without matches retries an empty match

quirks.description: The JIT only tries start positions where the code units at some fixed offsets fit the pattern, so a small (*LIMIT_MATCH=n) does not run out at positions the interpreter would try
quirks.case: pcre.json#JIT start search skips positions it never tries

quirks.description: Under the JIT, each branch holding a (*THEN) keeps a trap of three or more words on the JIT stack
quirks.case: pcre.json#JIT THEN trap holds stack words

quirks.description: Under the JIT a lookbehind with a variable-length branch sees its own position as the end of the subject (\z, $, \b and lookaheads inside it)
quirks.case: pcre.json#JIT ends the subject at a variable-length lookbehind

quirks.description: Under the JIT, backtracking into a non-atomic lookbehind that already succeeded retries it against the real end of the subject and continues where that retry ended
quirks.case: pcre.json#JIT resumes after a non-atomic lookbehind retried at the subject end

quirks.description: Under the JIT a variable-length lookbehind used as a condition only holds when its branch ends where the lookbehind started; pcre2_match() also accepts a branch that ends earlier
quirks.case: pcre.json#JIT holds a lookbehind condition to its end

quirks.description: Under the JIT a (*SKIP:NAME) without its (*MARK:NAME) ends a negative or conditional assertion like (*SKIP); the interpreter ignores it
quirks.case: pcre.json#JIT treats an unmatched SKIP name in a negative assertion as SKIP

quirks.description: The JIT stack overflows (PREG_JIT_STACKLIMIT_ERROR) after 4095 iterations of (?:a|b)* while a possessive repeat needs no stack
quirks.case: pcre.json#JIT stack overflows at 4096 iterations of (?:a|b)*

quirks.description: preg_last_error() keeps the previous error across calls that never reach a pattern
quirks.case: pcre.json#last error survives a call without patterns
